author: leopoldasch
text: @albrgr @lukeprog @moskov @mattyglesias Yep. The other issue is that the marg financial cost to additional quality-adjusted research here is super high, because it’s just so labor constrained atm.

author: leopoldasch
text: @albrgr @lukeprog @moskov @mattyglesias I generally share the skeptical reaction, but fwiw here’s a thought I had the other day: if generic R&D is already 50x-100x, is it that crazy that R&D targeted at a really neglected and high-stakes thing is 10-20x more levered and thus you get 1000x?

author: leopoldasch
leopoldasch
text: @albrgr @karthiktadepall There's another view of framing the uncertainty though (esp re longtermist impact), which is that there is a certain amount of value on the table, and then the uncertainty is over how much of the value is captured by, say, first 1/10th of the spending vs. rest.

author: leopoldasch
text: @albrgr @karthiktadepall The Weitzman point is quite under appreciated, more generally applies to trying to figure out what action-relevant eta is for philanthropic spending under uncertainty on eta...
